verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The Orion capsule has splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego... The splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. ET'; R2: 'splashed down off the coast of San Diego on April 10 just past 8 p.m. EDT'; R3: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact location, date, and time (8:07 p.m. EDT/ET on April 10, 2026, Pacific Ocean off San Diego).

verifications.claim: The splashdown occurred at 5:07 p.m. PDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '8 p.m. EDT / 5 p.m. PDT'; R3: '8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'; R5: 'splashdown at 5:07 p.m. Friday'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state the time as 5:07 p.m. PDT, matching the 3-hour difference from EDT.

verifications.claim: The capsule landed roughly 40-70 miles off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego'; R5: 'about 50-70 miles right off of San Diego's coast'
verifications.reasoning: Sources provide specific ranges (40-50 miles in R1, 50-70 in R5) that directly support the 'roughly 40-70 miles' claim; slight variation but precise match to location.

verifications.claim: A recovery team aboard the USS John P. Murtha recovered the four-person crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'flown to the flight deck of USS John P. Murtha'; R2: 'delivered via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha'; R3: 'safely aboard the USS John P. Murtha'; R4: 'now on the USS John P. Murtha, the recovery ship'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm the USS John P. Murtha as the recovery ship where the four-person crew was taken post-splashdown.

verifications.claim: The crew consisted of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Commander Reid Wiseman... Astronauts Christina Koch and Victor Glover...'; R2: 'Commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) mission specialist Jeremy Hansen'; R3: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen'
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names and affiliations (NASA for three, CSA for Hansen) listed identically across sources.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'after their historic 10-day trip to the moon'; R2: 'After 10 days and 695,000 miles'; R3: 'approximate 10-day mission'; R4: 'ending historic 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe the mission duration as 10 days, concluded by splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission marked the return of the first human flight to the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the first astronauts to journey around the moon in more than 50 years'; R6: 'the first crewed mission into deep space in more than 50 years'; R7: 'the first humans in over 50 years to venture to the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state it as the first human lunar mission (flyby/journey to Moon) in over 50 years since Apollo.
